question.text: The first Persian invasion of Greece was led by this Persian ruler in order to punish them for their participation in the Ionian Revolt. This man divided his empire into satraps.
question.clue: Near the end of his life, he ordered a large limestone rock to be inscribed with his genealogy in three languages; that inscription was translated into English in 1849.

swap.leadin: This ruler founded the Achaemenid [ah-KEE-men-id] Empire, which successfully grew by supporting local rulers as satraps and respecting local customs.
swap.text: Name this "Great" Persian ruler of the sixth century BCE who ended the Babylonian Captivity.
swap.clue: This victor of the Battle of Thymbra passed the Edict of Restoration, which granted the Jews religious tolerance, ending the Babylonian Captivity.

question.text: On Carter's last day in office, the signing of the Algiers Accords ended an event in this country. During that "hostage crisis" in this country, supporters of Ayatollah Khomeini invaded its U.S. embassy.
question.answerHtml: Iran [or Persia or Islamic Republic of Iran or IRI or Jomhuri-ye Eslâmi-ye Irân]
question.clue: 52 Americans were taken hostage in this country's capital during a "hostage crisis."

swap.text: The losing forces and Issus and Gaugamela were led by a ruler of this name, though he supposedly fled out of fear at both battles. Another ruler of this name fathered Xerxes the Great, and was Cyrus the Great's nephew.
swap.answerHtml: Darius [accept Darius III or Darius the Great or Darius I]
swap.clue: A successor of Cambyses II ("kam-BYE-zees the second") with this regnal name founded a capital at Persepolis.

question.leadin: After the Iberian War in 532, this empire signed the Perpetual Peace with a neighbor to its west.
question.text: Name this empire whose leader Khosrow I signed that treaty. Procopius, a neighboring empire's most famous historian, recorded that the treaty was broken within a decade in the Lazic War.
question.clue: This empire was defeated at Qadisiyyah at the hands of Umar's general, Khalid ibn al-Walid.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the general Belisarius.
swap.text: At the Battle of Dara, Belisarius defeated forces under this empire, who were known for their heavy armored horsemen called cataphracts. Later, the Byzantine Empire established the Eternal Peace with its leader Khosrau I (KHOO-shuh-roo "the first").
swap.clue: One king of this dynasty was crowned in utero, while another may have either flayed the skin of a noted captive or poured molten gold down his throat after forcing him and his army to work on an aqueduct, the Band-e-Kaisar.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Roman defeat at the Battle of Carrhae.
question.text: This Iranian empire defeated Rome at the Battle of Carrhae. They won the battle partially through the use of their namesake "shot," which involved horse archers firing behind them while retreating.
question.clue: This empire's namesake "shot" consisted of turning around on horseback during retreat to fire at the advancing army.

swap.text: According to the Chronicle of Early Kings, Sargon defeated an attempted invasion by four "great" generals from this polity, which was led by the King of Awan.
swap.clue: The "Lament for Ur" describes a conquest by these people, whose Shutrukid dynasty later defeated the Kassites and looted the stele bearing the Code of Hammurabi from Babylon.

question.text: This non-Persian empire of Iran was conquered by Cyrus the Great before he went on to conquer Lydia and Babylon, aided by a defector from this empire, Harpagus. Its last king was Astyages and its capital was Ecbatana.
question.clue: As a result of a battle at the Halys River, that waterway was declared its border with Lydia.

swap.leadin: The Hall of Hundred Columns in this city has the same dimensions as Athens's Odeon.
swap.text: Identify this ceremonial capital in the Zagros Mountains, home to the Apadana Palace built by Darius I.
swap.clue: In this home of a hundred-columned throne room, the Gate of All Nations led to the apadana palace.

question.text: In 305, Chandragupta secured the western boundaries of his nascent empire by defeating this eastern successor to Alexander the Great and then bribing him with 500 elephants.
question.clue: He dispatched the ambassador Megasthenes on expeditions to the east, resulting in the production of theIndika.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about elite military units from the Middle East.
swap.text: This empire was served by an elite detachment of 10,000 soldiers called the Immortals. Cyrus the Great ruled this empire that is called by either the name of its legendary ancestor or its origins in modern-day Fars province.
swap.clue: Another ruler of this empire used camels to win the Battle of Thymbra against Croesus of Lydia, and overthrew the earlier Median Empire.

question.text: Many Neo-Hittite states to the south spoke this Semitic language that replaced Akkadian to become the lingua franca of the Near East
question.clue: Demons found in the Ginza Rabba were repelled using ceramic bowls with incantations in this language.

swap.text: The Royal Road allowed these provincial governors to rapidly receive orders from Susa, as Artaphernes had during the Ionian Revolt. Several Indo-Scythian or Saka rulers were known as the "western" branches of these governors.
swap.answerHtml: satraps [accept satrapy or satrapies; accept khshathrapa or khshathrapavan or kshetrapal; accept Western Satraps or Great Satraps or Mahakṣatrapa; prompt on client kings or vassals or viceroys or archons]
swap.clue: 26 positions with this title were established around 580 BCE, a number that later increased to 36 according to the Behistun Inscription.

question.text: This site northwest of Persepolis was the necropolis of the Achaemenid dynasty. It is also home to a square tower called the "Cube of Zoroaster" and includes several impressive rock reliefs.
question.clue: One relief at this site shows a man on horseback holding one man by the hand, and another kneeling before the rider.

swap.leadin: Austen Henry Layard discovered a tablet that calls Ashurbanipal an "avenger" in reference to his sack of this "great holy city."
swap.text: Name this capital of the Elamites along with Anshan in the Zagros Mountains, which later became the winter capital for the Achaemenids. Hammurabi's code was unearthed in this city.
swap.clue: A polity that called itself Haltamti transferred its capital from Anshan to this city, and this "great holy city" suffered a brutal sack by Ashurbanipal.

question.leadin: A ruler with this name founded and named a city which was the location of an academy that served as the inspiration for Baghdad's House of Wisdom.
question.text: Give this name of the son of Ardashir I, who captured the Roman emperor Valerian during his campaigns to expand the Sassanid Empire westward.
question.clue: A king with this name built a namesake city on the road between Estakhr and Ctesiphon.

swap.leadin: Its capital was known as Ecbatana to the Greeks, and was probably founded by Cyaxeres.
swap.text: Name this empire, whose last ruler Astyages was overtrown by Cyrus the Great.
swap.clue: The city of Nineveh was captured by his successor Cyaxares, who extended this kingdom's borders to the Halys river in Asia Minor.

question.text: The namesake of the dynasty, Sassan, was a priest of this Persian religion that worshipped Ahura Mazda and became the Sassanid state religion.
question.clue: This chief religion sponsored by the Indo-Parthians and Parthians. Today, practitioners of this religion in India are called Parsees.

swap.leadin: Little is known about this figure, but according to Plutarch, he was tall, and was very manly despite the "delicacy of his looks and effeminacy of his dress."
swap.text: Name this Spahbod who was sent by Orodes II to delay the Romans, but ended up defeating them instead, using horse-archers and camels to resupply the archers.
swap.clue: According to Plutarch's Parallel Lives, a commander fighting against this leader had to rescind an attempted charge when he saw that his soldier's "hands were riveted to their shields and their feet nailed through and through to the ground" by arrows.
